changelog: Zone bypass comes to the alarm page and the main controls page. On the Comfort Alarm page, a bypassed zone now shows as Bypassed with an orange tile, and pressing and holding a zone tile sets or clears its bypass -- a normal tap still opens the zone's details, so a stray tap cannot change anything. The alarm page also gains an Alarm & Trouble Status button opening a table of everything Comfort reports: what each item is, whether it is currently reporting a problem, and when it was last observed, with a clear notice if the report source has gone quiet. On the Comfort Entities page, the zone tiles get the same bypass display and hold-to-toggle, the Responses section drops the repeated 'Comfort' prefix and pressing a response now presses it on the panel, and a new Zone Bypass card lists every bypassable zone with its current state and Set/Clear buttons.
details: v51 folds the Comfort add-on's v1.0.11 UI bundle into the fleet and converges every unit's Comfort Entities (storage-mode) dashboard onto the current controls layout. Payload: 27 files -- 22 byte-identical to the copies v50 shipped, dashboards/alarm.yaml replaced, first_boot.sh changed, and 3 new: packages/comfort_am_status.yaml, dashboards/includes/alarm_status_button.yaml and dashboards/includes/alarm_status_view.yaml (the updater creates the includes/ directory as it writes). Alarm & Trouble Status: packages/comfort_am_status.yaml adds one MQTT sensor (name Comfort AM Status, unique_id cytech_comfort_am_status, topic cytech_comfort_mqtt/alarm/am_status, value = the status field, attributes rows/updated/started, expire_after 45 s, qos 1) that the add-on publishes from v1.0.11 onward; dashboards/includes/alarm_status_view.yaml appends a subview (path am-status, panel mode, back to the alarm page) rendering a table from that sensor: per AM/AR code -- decimal code, event name, whether the code triggers Home Assistant per the reporting policy, current status (Active / Cleared / Event received / Unknown), last observation time and the panel's own detail text, with per-device instances expanding into a collapsible section; when the sensor is not 'online' the table switches to an explicit monitoring-unavailable notice and marks values as last known, and before the add-on has ever published it says it is waiting for the updated add-on (on an older add-on the sensor simply never arrives and nothing errors). dashboards/includes/alarm_status_button.yaml adds an 'Alarm & Trouble Status' button beside the Comfort Message card to open the view. Bypass on the Comfort Alarm page (dashboards/alarm.yaml): both zones-grid blocks carry the bypass display -- a zone whose sensor.<zone>_bypass_status reads 'Bypassed' shows Bypassed as its state, an orange theme-aware tint (#ffb74d dark / #e65100 light) overrides the red/green state colours, the border becomes 2px dashed, and pressing and holding the tile presses the matching button.comfort_<zone>_(set|clear)_bypass to toggle the bypass while a normal tap stays more-info. This is the version user-confirmed live on the bench 2026-10-02; the fleet copy now carries it, so the development units stop reverting to the stock file on the next update. Comfort Entities convergence (first_boot.sh self-heals -- the dashboard is storage mode, so per the v33 rule bundled dashboards are never applied over it and an additive one-time ensure is the only fleet path): ensure_responses_card now gates on the entity registry FILE (the v34 gate curled the Supervisor API, which is refused with HTTP 401 from the context first_boot runs in, so the old card only ever appeared on hand-built dashboards) and ships the upgraded tiles -- custom:button-card, name with the 'Comfort ' prefix stripped, state hidden (a press button's state is only a last-press timestamp), tap calls button.press with the entity from the template (button-card v5 drops a plain service_data entity: this.entity_id -- the template form is the proven one), hold more-info; button.comfort_*_bypass is excluded (those belong to the Zone Bypass card) and any other include on the card is left untouched. New ensure_zones_card_upgrade structurally patches the Zones card's two auto-entities includes to the same bypass display as alarm.yaml; every anchor must match the bench-verified shape exactly or the card is left alone, and an already-upgraded card is a silent no-op. New ensure_zone_bypass_card appends the Zone Bypass card exactly once -- one row per bypassable zone (name, Bypassed/Not bypassed, Set/Clear buttons), rendered server-side from a Jinja template over the bypass status sensors so it self-populates, hiding zones that still carry a default 'ZoneNN' name -- gated on the registry listing bypass buttons. Backup discipline: .pre_v34_backup (state before this file was ever touched) and .pre_v51_backup (state before this release's changes), each written once and never overwritten; HA restarts only when a file actually changed (the update's own Core restart runs the new first_boot, and the one-time pass restarts once more when it changed something); every piece re-runs as a silent no-op. Verification: the three ensure bodies reproduce the bench's pre-change dashboard byte-for-byte (md5 6157c38a... -> f90ebbf9..., the exact bytes now live on the bench, applied and verified 2026-10-03), the committed bash functions were extracted and pass golden / deferred-gate / restart-trigger / idempotence scenarios, and the alarm-page includes and bypass tiles were live-validated on bench and office (AM status table rendered on both, 2026-10-02).
